newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Shanghai newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Shanghai newspapers - July 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major political and business stories in local newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Shanghai. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- SHANGHAI SECURITIES NEWS - The newspaper carries a commentary by the Financial Times, mouthpiece of the central bank, saying that natural market forces have cooled the stock markets rather than the series of administrative measures introduced since early May.
- A total of 50 foreign banks, half of them among the world's top 50 banks, have established their China branches in Shanghai.

- BUSINESS NEWS - Famous economist Ma Hong says economic reforms of the past five years have led to supply of consumer goods far exceeding demand, and have changed China from a sellers' to a buyers' market.

- Commentary warns against over-optimism about China's surging foreign trade surplus, saying China accounts for only a small part of rapidly-developing world trade. The surplus hit $17.77 billion in the first half of this year against $876 million in the same 1996 period.
